newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. approves final renewal of Liberia observer unit.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves final renewal of Liberia observer unit.

text.p: The Security Council on Friday unanimously approved a three-month renewal of the U.N. Observer Mission in Liberia (UNOMIL) until September 30, when it said it expected the four-year-old operation in the civil war-ravaged country to end.

Comprising now only 86 military observers and a seven-member medical unit, UNOMIL has been working with a 10,000-strong peacekeeping force called ECOMOG fielded by the Economic Community of West African States.

A peace accord signed in Abuja, Nigeria, last August ended a multi-sided civil war that erupted in December 1989. More than 150,000 people were killed and the country's mining and rubber economy devastated.
Elections are scheduled for July 19 and a new government is to be installed the following month.

The council resolution renewing UNOMIL called on the Liberian parties to implement fully all the agreements and commitments they had entered into and urged all Liberians to participate peacefully in the electoral process.

It stressed the importance of close coordination between UNOMIL, ECOMOG and the Liberian electoral mechanism, as well as the importance of ECOMOG's continuing to provide security for international personnel and logistic support for the election commission.
The resolution stressed the obligation of all states to comply strictly with an embargo on the delivery of weapons and military equipment to Liberia imposed in November 1992.
